items.content: 1801—I have just returned from a visit to my landlord—the solitary neighbour that I shall be troubled with.
items.explanation: The journal-entry opening of Wuthering Heights, 1847. The dry understatement ('troubled with') and diary format are hallmarks of 19th-century English fiction.

items.content: Below, the cities are scattered like broken jewelry across black velvet, each cluster of light a small human argument against the dark. The plane hums its indifferent note, suspended between worlds, and you press your forehead against the cold oval glass as though listening for something. Down there, people are eating dinner, arguing, falling asleep in lit rooms — all of it invisible, all of it implied by those trembling constellations. You have never felt so tenderly alone.

items.content: The fields unrolled past the smeared window like something half-remembered, green giving way to brown giving way to a silver thread of river that vanished before she could name it. She had stopped trying to read an hour ago, the book face-down on her knee, forgotten. There was a particular loneliness to moving through a landscape that had never heard your name, where the farmhouses and their quiet smoke belonged entirely to other lives, and you were simply a blur behind glass, passing through without permission.

items.content: The train announced itself long before it arrived, a low moan threading through the dark like something alive and searching. Lying still beneath the covers, she listened as the sound swelled and then passed, trailing off into the fields beyond the town. There was something both lonely and consoling about it — proof that the world was still moving out there, carrying its cargo of strangers through the sleeping night, indifferent and endless.
